package_info.package_manager: system package manager (e.g., apt, yum, pacman), source distribution
package_info.package_versions: all versions (distrotech/cups-filters, OpenPrinting/cups-filters, cups-browsed, libcupsfilters, libppd)
package_info.why_malicious: The packages contain vulnerabilities that allow unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) via network-exposed services, enabling attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected systems. The vulnerabilities are present in all previous versions and can be exploited remotely if the CUPS service is enabled and accessible, especially via UDP port 631 or DNS-SD.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: N/A (The report does not provide a specific code snippet, but describes a vulnerability allowing unauthenticated remote code execution via network requests to the CUPS service, typically on UDP port 631 or via DNS-SD.)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the CUPS service receives a specially crafted network request on UDP port 631 or via DNS-SD, the vulnerable code path allows arbitrary code execution, resulting in the attacker gaining remote control over the system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Allowing unauthenticated remote code execution via a network service is highly suspicious and dangerous, as it enables attackers to compromise systems without credentials.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal CUPS operation should only process legitimate print service requests and never execute arbitrary code from unauthenticated network sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate remote management or print job submission should be authenticated and never allow arbitrary code execution.
key_indicators: Unauthenticated network access to a privileged service
Ability to trigger code execution remotely
Vulnerability present in default service configuration

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted network request to the CUPS service (typically on UDP port 631 or via DNS-SD).
attack_chain.leads_to: Triggering the vulnerable code path in the CUPS service.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable code path processes the malicious request and executes attacker-controlled code on the system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the target system, potentially leading to full system compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Unauthenticated network requests to CUPS service resulting in abnormal process behavior
Unexpected child process creation by cupsd
Unusual file writes or modifications by the CUPS service
file_indicators: Unexpected binaries or scripts created in /tmp or other writable directories by the CUPS service
Modifications to CUPS configuration files without administrative action
network_indicators: Inbound traffic to UDP port 631 from untrusted sources
Unusual DNS-SD traffic targeting CUPS service
Outbound connections initiated by the CUPS service to external IPs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unauthenticated or malformed network requests to the CUPS service, especially on UDP port 631 or via DNS-SD. Watch for abnormal child process creation or file modifications by the cupsd process. Use intrusion detection systems to flag exploit attempts targeting CUPS vulnerabilities (CVE-2024-47177, CVE-2024-47176, CVE-2024-47076, CVE-2024-47175). Block external access to UDP port 631 and monitor for signs of exploitation in system and application logs.
